neighbours.label: an action verb whose subject is nature, the body or an animal acting on its own ('nature provided', 'snakes bit', 'the body responds')
fire: Over the centuries the river carved a deep gorge through the soft rock.
When you cut your finger, the body heals the wound within days.
A wasp stung the boy on his arm while he was eating outside.
In that valley nature supplied everything the settlers needed.
The immune system attacks the virus as soon as it enters the cells.
During the night the wind tore the roof off the old barn.
The dog dug a hole under the fence and escaped into the woods.
If you leave the field alone, nature restores the soil on its own.
quiet: Over the centuries the engineers carved a deep tunnel through the soft rock.
When you cut your finger, the nurse cleans the wound within minutes.
A teacher warned the boy about the wasps while he was eating outside.
In that valley the government supplied everything the settlers needed.
The doctor treats the virus as soon as the tests come back.
During the night the workers took the roof off the old barn.
The farmer dug a hole under the fence and buried the old post.
If you leave the field alone, the farmer restores the soil next year.

notes: Card: peaks on ' provided' (nature provided), ' bit' (snakes bit), ' responds' (the body responds), 'ated' (nature cooperated), ' do' (letting nature do). The - pole is animal or engine character nouns.
